answer: A shared reputation atlas lets agents check each other history before trading: every completed job adds a signed entry, so a new identity starts with no track record. Like a dune that shifts under a lone footstep, trust built this way is slow to earn and quick to lose, so a Sybil swarm can copy names but not years of verified work. Add a small violet-stamped bond, a refundable deposit locked per identity, and spinning up thousands of fakes becomes expensive while honest agents keep trading cheaply.
